In all other aspects of management, the Act encourages State/Federal cooperation. Section 2 of the proposed legislation provides the mechanism for removal from the endangered list those species which have been restored to a status no longer endangered. Thereby, species under protection of Federal law because of their classification as endangered would then be returned to protection under State law. Protection of endangered species under Federal law assures uniformity of regulation from State to State of species whose ranges transcend State boundaries. Few of the State endangered species laws now in existence cover all endangered vertebrates and those which protect mollusks and crustaceans, as would the Federal law, are exceptional.
Emphasis on Protection. Several States expressed the opinion that the proposed legislation put more emphasis on protection and use restriction than on management. The Montana Department of Fish and Game says of the impact statement, "there seems to be strong emphasis toward 'restricting man's economic and cultural use of endangered species until the species are restored to productive levels,' and only minor emphasis on managing the habitat that produces the species of wildlife in question. If we are to actually save the wildlife this Act is purportedly concerned with, this emphasis must first be reversed."
The <u>Washington</u> Department of Game notes, "The general thesis of the draft emphasizes protection aspects as major means of accomplishing the goal of improving the status of endangered species.
